title: Triskaidekaphilia (Revisited): On the Contributions of James Bentley
content: After earning his Ph.D. in 1974 from Birmingham University, UK, James Bentley began his professional career as an electron microscopist at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. He was hired into ORNL as a research staff member to investigate radiation effects in molybdenum and vanadium alloys. He did this and performed transmission electron microscopy (TEM) in materials science at ORNL until his retirement in 2010. Over this 36-year span, Jim became a recognized expert and leader in electron microscopy that combined imaging and spectrometry, that is, analytical electron microscopy (AEM). His career included numerous collaborations with researchers at other federal laboratories, universities, and industry. He particularly enjoyed those that permitted long-term relationships to be formed with principal investigators and especially graduate students. For such collaborations, he was appointed Adjoint Professor of Materials Science, Dept. of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Vanderbilt University, and Adjunct Professor of Materials Science and Engineering, University of Tennessee, Knoxville. In addition to being both expert in the art and science of electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), Jim was known both for advancing the science surrounding these techniques and for working in partnership with manufacturers of the microscopes and the ancillary equipment used at the microscopes (e.g., spectrometers, cameras, detectors, pumps) to improve the performance of the hardware and later, the software.
